draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Siolim! This village on the Chapora River is the home of Zagor, a nocturnal vigil festival of dance, drama and music, and someone from here is called a Siolcar.
draft.hungryLine: There's no famous restaurant list for Siolim, so ask any Siolcar where they like to eat and follow their lead.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Pretty, green Oxel is about an 18 min walk north, and the Zagor site is roughly 24 min away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down to the Chapora River on the west side of the village and look across to Morjim and its pine-wooded beach.
moodReplies.surprise-me: A person from Siolim can be called a Siolcar, or even Shivalkar, Xivolkar in Konkani.

spots.name: Oxel
spots.detail: 18 min walk · A small, green village surrounded by water

spots.name: Zagor
spots.detail: 24 min walk · Siolim's famous nocturnal vigil of dance, drama and music

legends.title: The night of Zagor
legends.body: Zagor means a nocturnal vigil, and Siolim is where it is mainly celebrated. The festival brings dance, drama and music together through the night.

tips.title: Stay up late for Zagor.
tips.body: It's a nocturnal vigil, so the dance, drama and music happen through the night.

tips.title: Take the bridge across the Chapora.
tips.body: A bridge over the Chapora now stands where the old ferry used to run.

story.title: A river village
story.body: Siolim grew up around the Chapora River, with green hillocks towards Assagao and the quiet village of Oxel to the north.

story.title: Zagor nights
story.body: Siolim became known for Zagor, a nocturnal vigil festival of dance, drama and music.

story.title: Crossing the Chapora
story.body: People used to cross the Chapora by ferry. Today a bridge stands in its place.

story.title: A growing village
story.body: Siolim had 10,311 people in 2001 and 10,936 in 2011. It is split into wards called vadde, like Igrez-Vaddo and Gaunsa-Vaddo.
